name: L3Harris Technologies
description: L3Harris sells tactical radios and communications, electronic warfare, satellites and sensors, aircraft mission systems, and (via Aerojet Rocketdyne) rocket propulsion and missile components to the US Department of War, allies and some commercial customers. US government customers were 75 percent of fiscal 2025 revenue and 22 percent of revenue came from outside the US. It operates as a prime, a merchant supplier of components to other primes, or a subcontractor, and 75 percent of revenue is fixed-price. From fiscal 2026 it reports three segments instead of four. In April 2026 the Department of War agreed to invest $1 billion in the missile business (Aerojet Rocketdyne) through convertible preferred stock.

gics.note: Conventional label per Wikipedia's List of S&P 500 companies (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies, read 2026-10-01), which gives only the sector and the sub-industry; GICS industry group and industry are not shown there so are left null. Mowgli classification is not set here.

employees.note: Approximately 45,000 employees including about 18,000 engineers and scientists; hired about 6,000 in fiscal 2025. FY2025 10-K

businessLines.name: Space & Mission Systems (SMS)
businessLines.how: Government customers pay under development and production contracts for satellites, sensors and mission systems, mostly as a prime or subsystem integrator; revenue recognised as work is performed.
businessLines.description: Satellite and payload capabilities incl. missile warning and defense, with maritime, air special-missions and other defense and civil government programs (new 2026 segment).

revenue.note: H1 2025 $5,181M (recast to the new segments); Q2 2026 $2,966M vs $2,770M. Share is of the three segments summed before $173M intersegment eliminations.

businessLines.revenueNote: H1 2025 $5,181M (recast to the new segments); Q2 2026 $2,966M vs $2,770M. Share is of the three segments summed before $173M intersegment eliminations.

businessLines.name: Communications & Spectrum Dominance (CSD)
businessLines.how: Defense and public-safety customers and allied governments pay per radio and system delivered, plus upgrades and support; the highest-margin line, helped by international tactical-radio deliveries.
businessLines.description: Resilient communications (software-defined tactical radios, broadband, public safety radios) and electronic warfare combined into one segment (new 2026 segment).

revenue.note: H1 2025 $3,670M; Q2 2026 $1,943M vs $1,861M. Share is of the three segments summed.

businessLines.revenueNote: H1 2025 $3,670M; Q2 2026 $1,943M vs $1,861M. Share is of the three segments summed.

businessLines.name: Missile Solutions (MSL)
businessLines.how: Missile primes and the government pay per rocket motor and component delivered under multi-year production contracts (about 75 percent of Q2 revenue is as a subcontractor), plus space propulsion development work.
businessLines.description: Propulsion, sensing, guidance, fuzing and other missile and munition technologies (Aerojet Rocketdyne), plus space propulsion and power for national security space and NASA.

revenue.note: H1 2025 $1,765M; Q2 2026 $1,054M vs $925M. Share is of the three segments summed.

businessLines.revenueNote: H1 2025 $1,765M; Q2 2026 $1,054M vs $925M. Share is of the three segments summed.

brands.name: Aerojet Rocketdyne
brands.note: Operates as the MSL segment; subsidiary with a Department of War $1B preferred investment (Q2 2026 10-Q)

whatsNext.text: Qualified IPO of Aerojet Rocketdyne (the Missile Solutions business, via new subsidiary AXYV Inc.) if contractual milestones are met; otherwise the Department of War preferred stock carries 7% compounding dividends or is redeemable at fair value on 2031-04-17.
